Worked solution:

An arithmetic sequence is a sequence such that the difference of any two consecutive terms is the same (i.e. the common difference). So if we consider the 3 consecutive terms of the sequence \( ({@a_1@})\), \(({@a_2@})\), and \({@a_3@}\), we have that the difference between the second and first term must be equal to the difference between the third and second term: \[({@a_2@})-({@a_1@}) = {@a_3@}-({@a_2@}).\] Solving the equation for \(x\) we get

\({@a_2@} {@S1(-BB)@} {@S(-AA)@}x = {@a_3@} {@S(-CC)@}x {@S1(-DD)@}\)

\( {@CC*x@} {@S(-AA)@}x {@S(-EE)@}x {@S(CC)@}x = {@-DD@} {@S1(BB)@} {@S1(-DD)@}\)

\( {@(2*CC-AA-EE)*x@} = {@-2*DD+BB@}\)

\(x = {@ta1@}.\)

\(d= a_2-a_1= {@a_2_x@} - {@SP(a_1_x)@}= {@ta2@}\)
